question: For an i.i.d. distribution of exactly realizable, rank-deficient linear-regression tasks sharing one solution, can average past-task loss after sequential exact fitting be expressed and asymptotically characterized through the spectrum of a distribution-level projection operator?

key_findings.claim: The paper studies a stationary identification problem, not a general task-shift setting: every task is an i.i.d. draw from one distribution, all labels share the same exact parameter w-star, each task is fit exactly, and the model starts at zero.
key_findings.evidence: The iterate is the exact solution closest to the preceding iterate, equivalently an orthogonal projection of its error through the current task null space. There is no noise, target drift, finite-step SGD, replay, or changing task law.

key_findings.claim: The forgetting quantity is the expected average empirical loss on all tasks seen through horizon k, including a current-task term that is identically zero.
key_findings.evidence: F_Pi(k) averages losses from tasks 1 through k, while exact fitting makes loss_k(w_k)=0. Consequently the 1/k normalization and exact current-task fit are built into every reported rate; this is not peak forgetting, backward transfer, or a before-versus-after accuracy drop.

key_findings.claim: Theorem 3.1 gives an exact loss-level operator identity and Theorem 3.2 expands it into coupled spectral modes.
key_findings.evidence: With S_Pi(A)=E[P_t A P_t], the expected loss couples a future-propagated task covariance to a past-propagated target matrix around the current projector. Decomposing the self-adjoint operator into eigenspaces yields coefficients beta_rs and exact geometric sums Gamma_rs(k).

key_findings.claim: The top operator eigenvalue controls the generic asymptotic decay rate, but only when the loss and target activate its eigenspace.
key_findings.evidence: The leading coefficient can vanish. The paper distinguishes a generic c_top>0 term proportional to rho^(k-1), mixed top-mode terms with an additional 1/k factor, and lower spectral scales; at rho=1, O(1/k) behavior may reappear. Thus rho alone is not a complete prediction of nonzero forgetting.

key_findings.claim: The unconditional upper bound is F_Pi(k) no greater than ((k-1)/k) rho^(k-1) times target and task-scale factors.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.2 separates a distributional contraction rho from ||w-star w-star-transpose|| and E||C_t||. Calling this an unconditional exponential bound needs the qualification rho may equal one, in which case it provides no strict exponential contraction.

key_findings.claim: The spectral radius has a clear geometric interpretation as maximal average second-order survival under a random null-space projection.
key_findings.evidence: The Rayleigh quotient is E||P_t A P_t||_F^2/||A||_F^2. For a subspace projector it becomes an average of fourth powers of principal-angle cosines, linking slow contraction to directions nearly aligned with typical task null spaces.

key_findings.claim: Richer and more complementary tasks reduce the measured forgetting because they identify the shared solution faster, not because they prevent interference between changing targets.
key_findings.evidence: The paper explicitly interprets slow decay as slow approach to w-star and argues that increasing rank or diversity lowers rho. Under the shared-solution assumption, declining past loss is convergence to one common target, so retention and identification cannot be separated by this metric.

key_findings.claim: Commuting task families have exactly zero actual forgetting; the nearby (1-p_i)p_i^m expression is only a residual-surrogate term, despite being called a direction's finite-horizon forgetting contribution in the main text.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 4.6 proves F_Pi(k)=0 for every k when all support projectors commute, because the final error remains in every seen task null space. Remark 4.4 nevertheless describes (1-p_i)p_i^m as a direction's contribution to forgetting. Appendix Proposition C.7 resolves the tension: that expression is the residual surrogate f_m and enters only an upper bound on F_Pi(k), not the actual loss, which remains identically zero.

key_findings.claim: Projector statistics cannot determine the magnitude of forgetting.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition C.10 rescales every task as (X,y) to (epsilon X, epsilon y), leaving P_t, S_Pi, and rho unchanged while multiplying actual loss by epsilon squared. The loss-level covariance and target factors are therefore essential.

anchors.section: Proposition C.10 projector statistics are blind to loss scale

key_findings.claim: Empirical support is confined to two synthetic, realizable linear task families and does not include uncertainty intervals or neural/real-data validation.
key_findings.evidence: The main study uses d=192, rank 48 and one sampled unit target per alpha sweep rather than repeated target directions. The spike study averages 400 trajectories at seven separately simulated horizons; the richness sweep uses 24 sequences per point and estimates rho from 32 projectors. The plots report curves without confidence intervals, between-family replication, or hypothesis tests.

key_findings.claim: The experiments do not test the theorem's activation coefficient or distinguish a generic top-mode rate from a vanishing-coefficient case.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 1a-1c compare empirical forgetting, an upper bound, local slopes, and rho, but never estimate c_top or the top eigenspace projection. Appendix E explicitly says c_top requires estimating the top eigenspace and projecting both task covariance and target matrices and is numerically more delicate than estimating rho. Therefore Figure 1c validates a qualitative richness association, not generic top-mode activation.

anchors.section: E Practical estimation of rho and c_top

key_findings.claim: The paper reports operation-count and storage complexity for estimators but no measured wall-clock or systems cost.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix lists O(N K_max d r) rollout cost and O(T M d^2 r) power-iteration cost with O(M d r+d^2) storage for dense operator estimation. These are analytic counts, not timing, accelerator-memory, or energy measurements.

method.core_idea: Lift the random exact-fit error projection into a self-adjoint operator on symmetric matrices so that expected past-task loss can be written exactly and analyzed through its eigenspaces.
method.mechanism: Each task maps the error through P_t=I-X_t^+X_t. Independence lets future and past products be averaged into powers of S_Pi(A)=E[P_t A P_t]. The exact loss identity keeps the task covariance C_t and target outer product X-star inside the operator chain. An eigenspace expansion yields mode-coupling coefficients, asymptotic cases, an operator-norm upper bound, and a principal-angle interpretation. Synthetic task families test scale, local rate, and task richness.
assumptions: Every task is rank-deficient and exactly realizable by the same fixed parameter w-star.
Tasks are independent and identically distributed from one stationary law Pi.
Each task is trained to exact interpolation and selects the exact solution closest to the preceding iterate.
The initial model is exactly zero.
The moments used in the loss identity, including E||C_t||_F, are finite.
Sharp rho-rate conclusions require rho<1 and nonzero activation of the top eigenspace.
The model is linear, noiseless, and has known task boundaries; no replay or finite-step optimizer is modeled.

techniques.role: Expresses each sequential task update as an orthogonal error projection.
Averages P A P over the task distribution and closes past/future expectations.
Retains covariance scale and target activation rather than bounding only state residuals.
Decomposes forgetting into beta-weighted geometric sums across operator eigenspaces.
Interprets the top rate through fourth powers of angles to task null spaces.
Exhibits nontrivial laws with zero loss and rules out positive universal lower bounds.
Approximates forgetting and rho using sampled trajectories, low-rank projectors, and power iteration.

evaluations.setting: Shared-null-spike synthetic tasks with d=192, rank 48, alpha in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, seven horizons through 256, and 400 i.i.d. trajectories
evaluations.metric: Expected average past empirical loss and adjacent-horizon local decay rate
evaluations.result: The explicit bound has the predicted exponential ordering and the adjacent-horizon local rate approaches the analytic rho after transients, but the bound is not uniformly tight: for the slower alpha regimes it sits visibly far above empirical forgetting at long horizons
evaluations.baseline: A coarse projection-based O(1/k) upper bound and analytic rho

evaluations.setting: Angle-richness reservoir family with 30 richness values from 144 to 191, fixed 30-degree angle, horizons through 1024, 24 sequences per point, and 32 projectors per rho estimate
evaluations.metric: Long-horizon forgetting and estimated spectral radius
evaluations.result: Increasing task-family richness lowers both estimated rho and empirical k=1024 loss in the displayed sweep; this is qualitative association from 24 sequences and 32-projector point estimates, not a direct check of c_top activation or asymptotic goodness of fit
Forgetting rollouts cost O(N K_max d r); empirical-operator power iteration costs O(T M d^2 r) with O(M d r+d^2) storage
evaluations.baseline: Analytic closed forms when a structured family permits them

limitations: Author-stated and structural: conclusions are for overparameterized, noiseless, exactly realizable linear regression with a shared solution.
Reviewer-identified from the setup: the i.i.d. task law excludes nonstationary task distributions, changing targets, adversarial order, recurrence shifts, and state-dependent sampling.
Reviewer-identified from the update rule: exact fitting excludes finite data passes, optimization error, stochastic-gradient noise, regularization, and early stopping.
Reviewer-identified empirical scope: there is no replay buffer, memory-budget comparison, backbone, real dataset, or neural-network validation.

Reviewer-identified metric qualification: the metric includes a zero current-task term and measures average empirical loss rather than standard maximum forgetting, backward transfer, or population risk.
Reviewer-identified evaluation gap: no forward-transfer or unseen-task generalization metric is reported.
Author-stated theorem qualification: top-rate identification is conditional on coefficient activation; rho alone does not imply nonzero loss.
Reviewer-identified statistical and systems gap: experiments provide no confidence intervals, repeated target/family draws, formal goodness-of-fit test, or measured compute time.
Reviewer-identified theorem-to-experiment gap: c_top and its activation are never estimated, so the plots do not distinguish the generic rho rate from a coefficient-degenerate case.

Reviewer-identified presentation conflict: Remark 4.4 calls (1-p_i)p_i^m a forgetting contribution even though Appendix C.7 defines it for residual surrogate f_m and Proposition 4.6 proves actual forgetting is zero for commuting laws.
Reviewer-identified bound qualification: Figure 1a supports rate ordering but the explicit upper bound can remain visibly far above empirical loss at long horizons.
Author-stated Appendix C.10 qualification: projection statistics are invariant to loss rescaling and cannot by themselves quantify practical severity.
failure_modes: Commuting task projectors yield exactly zero loss even with nontrivial spectral survival.
A target orthogonal to the top eigenspace makes the leading coefficient vanish and changes the asymptotic scale.
When rho equals one, the nominal exponential factor does not contract and mixed modes may produce only a 1/k law.
Nearly invisible directions make rho approach one and require horizons on the order of effective dimension divided by visible rank.
Rescaling X and y makes forgetting arbitrarily small or large without changing any projector-only diagnostic.
Noisy or inconsistent tasks destroy the shared exact-solution projection recursion.
Correlated or distribution-shifting tasks break the independence step used to replace projection products with powers of one operator.
A finite Monte Carlo operator can misestimate a near-one top eigenvalue, especially when the eigengap is small.
reusable_insights: Keep loss scale and target activation inside a transfer-operator analysis; projector contraction alone is insufficient.
Separate a rate parameter from its activation coefficient before claiming asymptotic behavior.
Use commuting or jointly diagonalizable cases as mandatory counterexamples for universal forgetting bounds.
Label residual-surrogate terms separately from actual loss: a positive projector-chain residual can upper-bound an identically zero forgetting metric.
Distinguish retention from identification when all tasks share one solution and richer tasks improve both.
Report standard CL metrics alongside average empirical past loss so normalization and zero-current-task effects are visible.
Estimate spectral radii with eigengap and finite-sample uncertainty, not only a point power-iteration value.
Test any spectral diagnostic under target rotation, covariance rescaling, task correlation, noise, and nonstationary laws before generalizing it.
open_questions: Can an analogous operator close the loss dynamics for correlated or Markov task streams?
What replaces the exact identity under noisy, inconsistent, or task-specific teachers?
Can finite-step SGD, ridge regularization, replay, or momentum be incorporated without losing tractable spectral structure?
How does rho relate empirically to standard backward transfer and maximum forgetting in neural networks?
What finite-sample confidence bounds are available for estimating rho and its activation coefficient near a small eigengap?
Can task-boundary-free online estimates distinguish benign shared-solution identification from destructive target drift?
Do real representation spaces exhibit approximately commuting projectors, making the zero-forgetting edge case practically relevant?

competitive_landscape.title: How catastrophic can catastrophic forgetting be in linear regression?
competitive_landscape.difference: Analyzes a fixed jointly realizable task collection under cyclic and random orderings, whereas this paper samples an unbounded i.i.d. stream and derives a distribution-level matrix operator identity.

competitive_landscape.title: Theory on Forgetting and Generalization of Continual Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct theoretical comparator on arbitrary task sequences
competitive_landscape.difference: Provides expected forgetting and generalization expressions plus real-data DNN checks; this paper narrows to a shared exact teacher but gives a distribution-operator spectrum and sharper stationary asymptotics.

competitive_landscape.title: Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting for Random Orthogonal Transformation Tasks in the Overparameterized Regime
competitive_landscape.difference: Studies two orthogonally related tasks and validates with Permuted MNIST; this paper permits arbitrary i.i.d. projector laws but supplies only synthetic linear validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Forgetting in Continual Learning with Linear Regression
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct comparator covering SGD and task ordering
competitive_landscape.difference: Handles finite-step SGD in under- and overparameterized regimes and exposes covariance-order and stepsize effects; this paper assumes exact fitting and removes order through an i.i.d. law.

competitive_landscape.title: The Joint Effect of Task Similarity and Overparameterization on Catastrophic Forgetting -- An Analytical Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Derives exact two-task results for random orthogonal transforms and a nonmonotonic similarity effect; this paper studies long i.i.d. horizons through a general projection operator.

competitive_landscape.title: Theoretical Insights into Overparameterized Models in Multi-Task and Replay-Based Continual Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Characterizes buffer size, transfer, and generalization under replay and multi-task learning; this paper offers an exact no-replay spectral law but does not audit memory or forward transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: From Continual Learning to SGD and Back: Better Rates for Continual Linear Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Derives universal random-order rates with and without replacement for a fixed jointly realizable collection; this paper derives law-specific exponential behavior and exact spectral coefficients for i.i.d. draws.

competitive_landscape.title: Optimal L2 Regularization in High-dimensional Continual Linear Regression
competitive_landscape.difference: Studies high-dimensional population generalization with label noise, multiple teachers, and optimal isotropic regularization; this paper studies unregularized, noiseless empirical forgetting with one teacher.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper shifts exact-fit linear forgetting from random order over a fixed collection to an i.i.d. task distribution and gives an exact loss-level operator identity, spectral expansion, and generic asymptotic rate.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The primary-source audit found extensive prior exact-fit, arbitrary-task, similarity, SGD, replay, regularization, and random-order theory, but no checked predecessor with this same loss-level distribution operator and activation-coefficient expansion.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The operator identity and coefficient-aware spectral characterization appear genuinely new within the narrow shared-solution exact-fit model. The contribution should not be generalized to catastrophic forgetting under target drift, noisy tasks, neural training, or memory constraints; in this setting, much of the decay is shared-target identification.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification independently reread all 28 pages of the pinned arXiv v1 PDF (submitted 2026-04-15), including Theorems 3.1-4.2, Propositions 4.3/4.6 and their proofs, all Appendix C counterexamples, Appendix D algorithms, Figure 1 panels/captions, and Appendix E's estimator table. The source PDF and extracted-text SHA-256 values were recomputed and match fulltext_index exactly. Page anchors refer to PDF pages. Reviewer inferences are explicitly labeled: most importantly, shared-target identification is not changing-target retention; Remark 4.4's positive commuting-direction expression belongs to residual surrogate f_m rather than actual forgetting; and Figure 1 does not estimate c_top. Eight competitor mechanisms and their current official versions were rechecked on primary arXiv/PMLR records. Task boundaries are exact and known; replay budget is zero; the oracle is the shared exact teacher; uncertainty, forward transfer, state shift, and task-law shift are absent; compute is analytic rather than measured.

verification.passage_check: Re-read and cross-checked all 28 pinned PDF pages against the extracted text, including the exact projection recursion; Theorems 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, and 4.2 and their full proofs; Propositions 4.3 and 4.6; Appendix C residual bounds, commuting/rank-one/Haar families, and the C.10 rescaling counterexample; both synthetic protocols; Figure 1 and Table 1. Recomputed both source hashes. Corrected the main-text Remark 4.4 boundary by checking Appendix C.7: (1-p_i)p_i^m is f_m, whereas Proposition 4.6 makes actual forgetting exactly zero. Also checked current-task normalization, rho=1 and vanishing-coefficient cases, one-target experimental replication, bound looseness, and the absence of c_top estimation.
verification.competitor_check: Inspected current official primary records for PMLR v178/evron22a, v202/lin23f, v206/goldfarb23a, v235/ding24c, v313/evron26a, and v313/karpel26a, plus arXiv 2401.12617v2 and 2408.16939v2. Checked titles, versions/venues, exact-fit versus finite-step mechanisms, fixed-collection versus i.i.d. task sampling, evaluation scope, replay/regularization/noise assumptions, and rate/geometry claims; the target paper was excluded. The closest same-year rate comparator remains Evron et al. (ALT 2026), while none of the checked records supplies the same loss-level distribution-operator expansion with target-activation coefficients.
